newsitem.title: CHINA: China smelters actively bought zinc options - trade.
newsitem.headline: China smelters actively bought zinc options - trade.

text.p: Chinese smelters with large open short positions in zinc on the London Metal Exchange (LME) have recently been actively establishing fresh option positions in the metal, traders said.

Chinese and Western trading sources interviewed ahead of a dive in zinc prices on Tuesday said China had been buying zinc options on the LME for "decent tonnages" at strike prices between $1,400 and $1,700 a tonne.
"We have done some decent buying of call options for different tonnages, with strike prices around $1,500 and $1,650," said a source close to metals authorities in Beijing.
He declined to say what tonnages had been purchased.
He did say, however, that one Chinese smelter had sold call options when the zinc price was $1,200 a tonne, earlier in the year, though he did not say at what price those options had been purchased.
A Western trader said Chinese buying had been seen in London last week when the zinc price was $1,520 a tonne.
Three-month zinc plunged in active trade on the LME on Tuesday at one point shedding $300 in an hour from a seven-year high on Monday of $1,675 a tonne.
By 1230 GMT the metal had recovered from an early low of $1,370 to settle at $1,480.
Traders in London last week reported Chinese buying LME zinc call options equivalent to 10,000 to 12,500 tonnes of metal.
Asian traders said this was an insignificant amount, but it had led to increased market volatility. --Shanghai Newsroom (8621) 6279-8544
